articles.title: Wes Henderson Sued: Angel's Envy Co-Founder Accused of Secretly Recording Intimate Moments of Around 40 People
articles.description: Angel's Envy co-founder Wes Henderson faces a civil lawsuit from family members alleging he secretly recorded around 40 people using hidden cameras. His attorney 'unequivocally denies the allegations in the lawsuit'. Wes Henderson, co-founder of the Angel's Envy whiskey brand, Kentucky Bourbon Hall of Fame inductee and owner of the Kentucky Castle hotel in Versailles, is facing a civil lawsuit filed by family members who allege he used hidden cameras to secretly record around 40 people without their consent. The complaint, first filed in Oldham County, Kentucky, claims the recordings were made across several locations, including his private homes and the Kentucky Castle hotel. Henderson has denied the claims through his attorney, and no criminal charges have been publicly reported so far. His attorney said Henderson 'unequivocally denies the allegations in the lawsuit' and added that the defense expects the case to be either voluntarily dismissed or fought hard in court. Wes Henderson Sued Over Alleged Hidden Camera Recordings How The Cameras Were Allegedly Found According to the filing, family members spotted about 15 disguised cameras during a stay at Henderson's Florida home in June 2025. A later search of his Oldham County residence allegedly turned up roughly 15 more recording devices. Nebraska S*x Trafficking Bust: Gujarati Woman Used Hidden Hotel Cameras To Monitor S*xual Abuse of 2 Teenage Girls Live. The plaintiffs claim the memory cards and footage they recovered show people undressing, using the restroom and being intimate. They also allege some cameras were pointed at beds, that cameras were placed inside homes belonging to third parties, and that some clips show s*xual activity at the Kentucky Castle hotel. The complaint further claims there is footage of Henderson himself with other women. Florida Therapist Has Secret S*xual Relationship With Patient, Arrested. Charges Listed In The Civil Complaint The suit lists counts of voyeurism, invasion of privacy, and viewing or possessing depictions of a minor in a s*xual performance. The last count relates to bathroom footage that allegedly features an unidentified person who appeared to be a minor. The plaintiffs also allege that Henderson sent multiple text messages over an 11-month period after being confronted, apologizing and asking for forgiveness. Police Role And Damages Sought The plaintiffs say they handed the recovered equipment and digital recordings to law enforcement. Local agencies, however, indicated they were not actively involved in the civil case. The family is seeking punitive damages, compensation for pain and suffering and medical expenses, and has demanded a jury trial. Who Is Wes Henderson? Henderson co-founded Angel's Envy with his father, master distiller Lincoln Henderson. Bacardi bought the brand in 2015 in a deal reportedly worth about USD 150 million. He was inducted into the Kentucky Bourbon Hall of Fame in 2019, later bought the 53-acre Kentucky Castle property in Versailles and launched the True Story whiskey brand. (The above story first appeared on LatestLY on Oct 03, 2026 07:44 AM IST. For more news and updates on politics, world, sports, entertainment and lifestyle, log on to our website latestly.com).

articles.title: Former WSU Student Receives Maximum Jail Sentence For Secretly Recording Men In Campus Shower
articles.description: The 20 year old former Washington State University student convicted of secretly taking videos of men inside a dorm shower and bathroom has received the maximum jail sentence. Juan Velasco pleaded guilty in August to one count of felony voyeurism in Whitman County Superior Court. Velasco was initially charged with three counts for using his phone to secretly record men in the 3rd floor bathroom of Stephenson South in April of last year. The prosecutor's office dropped two counts partly because two of the victims could not be identified. One victim who was recorded in the shower was identified. Judge Roger Sandberg agreed with the prosecutor's request for the maximum sentence allowed by state law in this case. Judge Sandberg sent Velasco to jail for 3 months, ordered that he undergo a psychosexual evaluation and register as a sex offender for 10 years. The identified victim agreed with that sentencing recommendation. Velasco has been living in Toppenish since he was suspended by WSU. The case was investigating by the WSU PD.

articles.title: 'Peeping Tom gets out': Man who allegedly hid three spy cameras in Hong Kong gym changing rooms out on bail
articles.description: A Hong Kong man who allegedly installed pinhole cameras in changing rooms at a branch of a popular gym chain has been released on bail pending further police investigation to identify potential victims. Construction site foreman Fung Kwok-wang, 34, was not required to answer a count of voyeurism during his first appearance at Sha Tin Court on Tuesday, as prosecutors sought an eight-week adjournment for further police inquiries. Acting Principal Magistrate Cheang Kei-hong granted the defendant HK$2,000 (US$255) bail on condition that he remain in Hong Kong, avoid contact with prosecution witnesses and stay away from the 24/7 Fitness branch on Lek Yuen Street in Sha Tin. The case will be heard again on November 25. The fitness centre reported the case to police on Friday after a customer spotted a small camera secured with black tape in the false ceiling of a changing room. Police combed through the premises and seized three pinhole cameras and three 12GB memory cards from three of the four individual unisex changing rooms. Officers subsequently recovered multiple video clips filmed between September 23 and 25. Fung was arrested shortly after 9pm on Sunday. The Sha Tin district investigation team is handling the case. Voyeurism is punishable by up to five years in prison, which is capped at two years when the case is heard by a magistrate.

pendingReview.title: Homeland Security investigating Kentucky bourbon maker's alleged secret sex recordings
pendingReview.description: TKC Distilling fired Wes Henderson as CEO and named his son Kyle to lead. A federal investigation has begun into the secret videos allegedly recorded by Kentucky bourbon maker Wes Henderson. Henderson is a member of the Kentucky Bourbon Hall of Fame and is best known as the founder of Angel's Envy, which he sold to Bacardi in 2015 for a reported $150 million. He has been removed from the Angel's Envy website as well as from his leadership role at The Kentucky Castle, a wedding venue, hotel and restaurant in Woodford County, where people allegedly were secretly recorded having sex. Versailles Police Chief Rob Young said on Monday that Homeland Security investigators in Louisville have the evidence and "are going through a large volume of material." Young said that as of Monday morning, he was told "no victims have been identified from the Kentucky Castle," the hotel, restaurant and venue in Woodford County. "If any victims from the castle are identified, Versailles police will coordinate with Homeland Security," Young said. No charges have been filed against Henderson. Homeland Security officials were not immediately available to comment. This story will be updated as more details become available. Hidden cameras found by family members The recordings came to light after family members, staying at a Florida vacation home owned by Henderson in June 2025, allegedly discovered at least 15 hidden cameras, some with Wifi capabilities, positioned in bedrooms and bathrooms, according to a lawsuit filed in Oldham Circuit Court. More hidden cameras were later found at Henderson's home in Oldham County, according to the filing, and footage allegedly showed Henderson installing cameras on third-party homes, which were not identified in the filing. The lawsuit, which has been sealed, was filed in June by family members against Henderson, accusing him of voyeurism, invasion of privacy and possession or viewing or matter portraying a sexual performance by a minor. The court filing says some underage family members were captured on the cameras nude. The evidence, including cameras and SD cards, was turned over to "local authorities" in December, according to the filing. It has been unclear, until now, who was in possession of the materials and might be investigating. Family members have not responded to requests for comment. On Friday, an attorney for Henderson issued a statement saying: "Wes unequivocally denies the allegations in the lawsuit. It is our understanding that the complaint will be voluntarily dismissed. If that does not happen, he is prepared to vigorously defend himself." The lawsuit appeared to still be active as of Oct. 5. On Saturday, the parent company that owns The Kentucky Castle, TKC Distilling, announced that it has terminated Henderson as CEO, effective immediately, and has named his son, Kyle, formerly the COO, to run both the Kentucky Castle and True Story Whiskey. "The Board will conduct a full and independent investigation into the allegations," it said in a statement. "The company remains committed to addressing the matter responsibly and to ensuring that the investigation is conducted thoroughly and fairly." The attorney for the company said Monday: "TKC Distilling will fully cooperate with any and all legal investigations." Henderson, who has taken a leave of absence from his role as a deputy coroner in Oldham County, has not commented publicly. Recordings from the Kentucky Castle Henderson has owned the Kentucky Castle since 2023. He is facing multiple lawsuits for debts related to his distilling and hospitality businesses. According to the filing in Oldham County, some of the recordings showed people at the Kentucky Castle. The filing did not identify a timeframe for when the recordings were made. In a footnote, the filing noted, "Some of the videos were from SD cards that captured sex at the Kentucky Castle which is connected to a business interest of the Defendant Wes Henderson." "The cameras also captured the defendant, Wes Henderson, having sex with other women (not his wife). Upon information and belief, the cameras captured other adults having sex, as well as footage of what appeared to be a homeless individual, potentially a minor, who happened to be carrying a portable medical device, using the restroom," according to the filing. According to the filing, the cameras in the Melbourne, Fla., home were disguised as fire alarms, behind a mirror, in a fan, in a clock, in a speaker, in a bathroom air vent directly above the toilet, in charging blocks and plug outlet extenders, according to the filing. According to the filing, "there are a total of 40 people identified as being captured without their knowledge." Some of the footage included Henderson allegedly placing the cameras and deliberately placing them to capture views of a bed, according to the filing. In some videos, Henderson allegedly is wearing a firefighter's shirt while placing cameras, according to the filing. After he was confronted, Henderson allegedly had repeatedly apologized to family members for his actions "and requested forgiveness through several text messages to multiple members of his family," according to the filing.

pendingReview.title: HK privacy watchdog probes 24/7 Fitness after pinhole cameras found in changing room
pendingReview.description: Hong Kong's privacy watchdog has launched a probe into commercial gym chain 24/7 Fitness after pinhole cameras were discovered in the changing room of a Sha Tin branch. The Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data (PCPD) said on Monday that it had begun a compliance check on 24/7 Fitness and required the company to provide information about its security measures following the pinhole camera discovery. A staff member at a 24/7 Fitness branch in Sha Tin discovered pinhole cameras mounted on the ceiling in a changing room last month and filed a police report. A 34-year-old man was arrested and charged with voyeurism over the incident. The PCPD said the probe was intended to "ensure that the personal data privacy of 24/7 FITNESS members is adequately protected," adding that it would look into whether the security measures implemented by 24/7 Fitness are sufficient to prevent similar incidents from happening again. In a statement following the incident, 24/7 Fitness said it had implemented new procedures and stepped up checks across all branches for hidden cameras. The company said it had inspected the showers, changing rooms, and restrooms "to ensure members can use the facilities safely and with peace of mind." It had also suspended the suspect's membership and assisted with the police investigation, it said. The branch where pinhole cameras were found is located in Lek Yuen Estate in Sha Tin. 24/7 Fitness operates more than 160 gyms throughout Hong Kong.
